Title: Oil's long view darkens as Middle East war refuses to end
Article:
OIL markets initially treated the Iran war as a brief bullish disruption in a long-term bearish trend. But traders are now betting that oil prices will remain elevated through 2028, forcing a rethink of the global inflation outlook.
Eight months into the war, the buffers that helped absorb the initial energy shock — most notably onshore crude oil stockpiles — are wearing dangerously thin. At the same time, the recovery in crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz remains fragile, global refining capacity has been eroded and credible diplomatic pathways to end the conflict appear narrower than ever.
Global benchmark Brent crude futures tell the story. Contracts for delivery in December next year have climbed more than 13 per cent since the start of September to US$86 a barrel, the highest level for the contract, while this December, contracts have gained around 12 per cent.
The Brent forward curve is not a price forecast, of course. But it reflects the willingness of refiners, airlines, commodity traders and asset managers to lock in elevated prices months and even years into the future.
In effect, market participants are paying a premium against the possibility that today's disruptions will become tomorrow's normal.
This market positioning stands in stark contrast to widely held industry expectations of a recovery in global oil supplies next year.
The International Energy Agency projects global supply will rise to 108.3 million barrels per day (bpd) next year from 100.7 million bpd this year as Middle Eastern exports recover.
Demand, meanwhile, is forecast to increase from 102.4 million bpd to 104.4 million bpd next year, still slightly below last year's consumption.
This recovery is expected to be concentrated in petrochemical feedstocks rather than transportation fuels like diesel.
Regardless, the agency's projected balances imply a sizeable supply surplus next year that would normally weigh on prices.
Yet the steady rise in long-dated futures suggests investors are increasingly sceptical that this recovery will fully materialise or, if it does, that it will endure.
The standoff between Washington and Teheran remains centred on control of the Strait of Hormuz.
The conflict has also expanded beyond the Gulf. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have recently stepped up missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes last week on the headquarters of state-owned oil giant Aramco in Dhahran.
Given this backdrop, every barrel leaving the Gulf now carries a widening security premium.
Absent a durable settlement over Hormuz, much of that cost is likely to remain entrenched in prices for the foreseeable future.
The strain is even more visible in diesel markets.
Benchmark European diesel futures hit a record US$1,480 per metric tonne, equivalent to about US$210 per barrel, in mid-September amid an acute shortage of supplies caused by disruptions in the Middle East and Russia.
Since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, drone attacks by Kyiv have crippled Russian refineries, forcing Moscow to ban diesel exports earlier this year.
On Friday, United States President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to allow Moscow to resume some diesel exports and later proclaimed another "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine.
But the additional Russian exports cited by Trump are minuscule — equivalent to roughly 12 hours of global supply — and no one, including the two parties involved, is giving much credence to the purported ceasefire.
Fuel repricing may ultimately prove more important than the rise in crude itself.
Diesel powers the trucks, ships, factories and farms that underpin global commerce. Sustained diesel inflation has historically seeped into the wider economy through higher transportation, manufacturing and food costs.
For much of this year, energy markets operated on the assumption that the Iran war would resemble past geopolitical crises: a sharp but temporary disruption followed by a quick return to normality.
Increasingly, investors are concluding otherwise. The issue is no longer simply how much oil can move through Hormuz.
Markets need to know whether the global energy system can quickly rebuild the inventories, refinery capacity and supply chains damaged by months of conflict.
Until then, the world risks becoming trapped in an era of structurally higher energy costs that lasts long after the shooting stops.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Detained Suu Kyi receives UK royal package: Myanmar govt
Article:
YANGON: Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi received a package from Britain's King Charles III on Monday, authorities said, releasing the first pictures of the detained Nobel laureate in two months and describing her as a "special female prisoner."
It is the first time Myanmar authorities have used the term to describe Suu Kyi, who was deposed in a military coup in 2021, triggering an ongoing civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people, according to monitor ACLED.
The coup leader and former junta chief Min Aung Hlaing was installed as civilian president in April following elections that did not include Suu Kyi's party, and she was moved to house arrest soon afterwards.
Home ministry officials met her on Monday to deliver a package of two books about soil, "one sealed envelope, and a sealed diplomatic communication sent by King Charles III of the United Kingdom to the special female detainee", Myanmar's presidential spokeswoman said on her Facebook page.
Britain is Myanmar's former colonial power and the monarch is known to have a keen interest in gardening and the environment.
Accompanying the statement were two images of Suu Kyi meeting two men with their backs to the camera.
The pictures appeared to be in a similar room to the last released images of her, when she met a Red Cross representative in August, her first publicised meeting with a foreign official since her ouster.
Fact-checkers from AFP examined the latest photos and found no evidence of manipulation using Meta Generative AI or OpenAI tools.
Suu Kyi remains detained on charges rights groups say were concocted to return power to the military, which has historically ruled Myanmar since independence.
"I have been extremely lenient toward her," Min Aung Hlaing said in an interview with Time magazine published last month.
The Foreign Office in London did not immediately respond to questions from AFP asking whether British diplomats had sought to deliver the package in person, or been refused permission to do so.

Title: AI isn't Asia's only game in town
Article:
AS doubts mount over Asia's artificial intelligence boom, some of the region's strongest returns are building far from the hype.
While tech dominates the headlines, old-economy mainstays are also key drivers of the broader market story.
Technology accounts for six of Asia's 15 best-performing market sectors this year thus far. But the remaining nine tell a non-tech story anchored in financials, energy, industrials and process industries.
Admittedly, some of these themes overlap with the AI capital expenditure juggernaut. For example, investments in power generation, grid infrastructure and industrial cooling are clearly being propelled by data centre needs.
But AI is not the only driver of these old-economy investment sweet spots, as geopolitical unrest and high energy prices are also playing a role.
Fears about a slowdown in the tech boom may rattle Asian markets—as we saw last week—but they will not necessarily bring the Asian surge to a screeching halt.
Rising global defence spending has been a major investment driver worldwide this year, as military tensions escalate, most notably in the Middle East and Europe.
This trend has been building ever since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and has skyrocketed as United States President Donald Trump has put more pressure on European allies to increase defence spending.
North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato) members, which account for 65 per cent of global defence expenditure, committed in June last year to raise their annual defence spending to five per cent of gross domestic product by 2035. Global defence spending represented only 2.4 per cent of global GDP last year.
The widening conflict in the Middle East, which escalated following the US-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28, has also highlighted the vulnerability of Gulf countries.
Asian defence manufacturers stand to gain from this global defence spending boom as Western capacity constraints potentially give Asian rivals an edge in delivery times and prices for comparable equipment.
According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, South Korea supplied 8.6 per cent of all arms imported by European Nato members during 2021-2025, ahead of Israel's 7.7 per cent and France's 7.4 per cent.
This came as Europe's overall arms imports roughly tripled.
At the same time, "insourcing" of defence manufacturing—creating a homegrown military-industrial complex—is already a trend in several Asian nations.
India aims for 70 per cent defence "indigenisation" by next year, Indonesia seeks 60 per cent local content in defence equipment by 2030, and Vietnam is targeting 50 per cent domestic inputs in select armaments by 2030.
Increasing defence needs and military modernisation are also spurring a broader infrastructure buildout globally. This includes reinforced bridges, roads, ports and railways, which are needed to transport heavy equipment, alongside fortified energy grids, telecommunications services and cyber networks.
McKinsey forecasts US$106 trillion in global infrastructure investment through 2040, with Asia accounting for roughly 65 per cent of that.
The region's domestic industry has several advantages, including local ties, inexpensive state financing and integrated operations that can lower costs and speed delivery.
Asia's infrastructure buildout could be mammoth, too. Regional transport infrastructure alone could require investment of US$2.6 trillion annually through 2035, according to the Asian Transport Observatory and the Asian Development Bank.
The global drive for energy independence should also benefit Asia, the leader in clean energy technologies.
The stickiness of crude oil prices above US$100 a barrel—and the related shock closure of the Strait of Hormuz this year—should push more consumers, businesses and governments towards renewables, particularly solar power, battery energy storage, offshore wind and electric vehicles.
According to FactSet, Chinese electric vehicle makers BYD and Geely draw 43 per cent and 23 per cent of their respective revenue from abroad, while Chinese battery titan CATL generates 34 per cent of its revenue overseas.
Swapping AI exposure for heavy industry and state-backed defence does not eliminate risk—it merely trades tech valuation hype for other hazards.
Meanwhile, prolonged inflation, elevated energy prices and high interest rates could slow infrastructure buildouts and trigger corporate defaults.
And a truly massive AI pullback could have ripple effects across the region's markets.
Yet, for now, Asia's old economy continues to offer genuine substance beyond all the tech-driven hype.
Writing for Reuters, the writer is founder and CEO of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Indonesia probes 98 forest fire cases involving links to neighbouring countries
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian police have confirmed foreign involvement, including from neighbouring countries, in 98 corporate cases linked to the forest and land fires gripping the country.
National Police Chief General Suyudi Ario Seto said the Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) was working to identify those responsible and establish the nature of their involvement.
"Of the 98 corporate cases we are investigating, there is foreign involvement, but as the investigations are ongoing, we are still determining which involve foreign investment or foreign parties and which do not," he told a press conference after a limited Cabinet meeting with President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta on Monday.
Suyudi said investigators were gathering evidence and expected to name suspects soon, including company owners and shareholders who could be held responsible for the fires.
Separately, Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Dudung Abdurachman called for firefighting operations to be intensified without waiting for rainfall, stressing the need for immediate and sustained action.
"The president instructed that the deployment of troops and personnel, including the Indonesian military, police, Forestry Service and members of the public, be intensified.
"This must be carried out on a massive scale, in a measured manner and without delay, because the situation has become very disruptive," he said.
Dudung also said Indonesia had responded to offers of foreign assistance, including from Malaysia and Singapore, with the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) coordinating technical arrangements for the proposed support.
However, at an earlier press conference, he said foreign assistance would have to wait until the Indonesian government declared the fires a national disaster. The government has yet to take this step, maintaining that it can manage the crisis with its own resources.

Title: Meta apologises after suspending "No Kings" Instagram account
Article:
WASHINGTON: Meta apologised for suspending the Instagram account of the "No Kings" protest movement over the weekend, attributing the shutdown to a sharp increase in activity that looked like automated bot traffic rather than human exchanges.
Demonstrators gathered at thousands of events across the United States on Saturday decrying President Donald Trump's aggressive deportation efforts, war in Iran and other policies in the third round of the "No Kings" rallies.
The Instagram account used by organisers and attendees, however, was offline for more than an hour. And Meta spokesman Andy Stone wrote in a post on X that it took longer to fix problems with organisers' access to the accounts.
Stone said network security systems detected the use of a Claude tool reading profiles, posts, and hashtags, with the rate sharply increasing in intense bursts on Oct 17.
"These abrupt, high-volume, sequential requests in a short period resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems. This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline," he said.
"We want to reiterate our sincere apology for the error."
Rally organisers were not satisfied on Monday.
"Meta's explanation still doesn't add up," the No Kings Coalition said on the Bluesky platform. "Beyond shutting down our Instagram, we've received reports that NoKings and early voting content was inaccessible, restricted, or seemed suppressed across Meta platforms."
"Weeks before an election, an apology isn't enough. The public needs answers, accountability, and concrete safeguards," the coalition said.
"No Kings" rallies took place in cities from Seattle and San Diego to Chicago, Atlanta and New York. In Washington, DC, protesters gathered at the site of Trump's proposed triumphal arch to encourage early voting before the Nov 3 midterm congressional elections.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EPF, KWAP, Aberdeen pare CTOS stakes as shares plunge 44pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three major shareholders of CTOS Digital Bhd have collectively disposed of nearly 22 million shares since Sept 23, when the credit reporting agency disclosed a cybersecurity breach that has since sent its share price tumbling.
Bursa Malaysia filings showed that the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP) and Aberdeen Group plc have reported only disposals, with no acquisitions, during the period.
CTOS shares fell 15.29 per cent, or 6.5 sen, to close at a fresh record low of 36 sen today, after hitting an intraday low of 35.5 sen.
The latest decline brings the stock's cumulative loss to 44.19 per cent from its Sept 22 closing price of 64.5 sen, the last trading day before the cybersecurity disclosure.
CTOS was the eighth most actively traded counter on Bursa Malaysia, with 29.39 million shares changing hands, its highest daily trading volume in over three months.
Of the three institutional shareholders, KWAP recorded the largest reduction in its holdings, followed by EPF and Aberdeen.
KWAP's latest disposal involved 1.77 million shares on Oct 16, reducing its stake to 191.81 million shares, or 8.724 per cent. Its holdings have declined by about 10.99 million shares since Sept 25.
EPF, meanwhile, disposed of 1.31 million shares on Oct 14, bringing its holdings to 449.10 million shares, or 20.43 per cent. Its holdings have fallen by about 6.38 million shares since Sept 23.
Aberdeen's latest reported disposal involved 384,000 shares on Oct 14, leaving it with 325.22 million shares, representing a 14.79 per cent stake. Its holdings have declined by about 4.20 million shares since Sept 25.
The combined reduction of about 21.57 million shares represents roughly one per cent of CTOS's issued share capital.
Meanwhile, CTOS itself bought back 500,000 shares at 61 sen apiece on Sept 25, two days after disclosing the cybersecurity breach, for an estimated RM305,000.
The stock has since fallen nearly 41 per cent from that repurchase price to today's closing price of 36 sen.
CTOS first disclosed the breach on Sept 23, saying unauthorised access had been detected in an environment supporting its consumer business.
The company said certain files containing a limited subset of processed consumer information had been accessed, although the incident had been contained and other systems were unaffected.
At the time, CTOS said the breach was not expected to have a material financial impact.
However, on Oct 13, the company estimated that the disruption would reduce its profit after tax and minority interests by RM12 million and revenue by RM16 million for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
The estimates assumed that certain affected services, including CTOS Score and Central Credit Reference Information System-related reports, would remain unavailable until the third week of October.
CTOS also estimated that every additional week of disruption could reduce profit by RM1.3 million and revenue by RM2.5 million.
This has prompted several research houses to downgrade the stock and lower their earnings forecasts.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd and CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd downgraded CTOS to "Hold" from "Buy", while Kenanga Research lowered its recommendation to "Market Perform" from "Outperform".
Kenanga adopted a more conservative assumption that the affected services could remain unavailable until the end of December, potentially raising the profit impact to RM22 million.
RHB Research, however, maintained its "Buy" recommendation, arguing that the sell-off had been excessive given CTOS's established position in the credit reporting industry.
Analysts have also raised concerns that restoring the affected services may not immediately translate into a recovery in transaction volumes, with potential customer migration and higher cybersecurity spending posing risks to future earnings.
The sharp decline in CTOS shares has also coincided with the appointment of Putri Norlisa Najib, the daughter of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, as an independent non-executive director.
The stock gained one sen to close at 64.5 sen a day after her appointment was announced on Sept 21, before beginning its decline.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 17 arrested over ECRL, Telekom Malaysia cable thefts
Article:
TEMERLOH: Police have arrested 17 men suspected of belonging to four gangs linked to robberies and cable theft involving the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project and Telekom Malaysia in Temerloh.
Temerloh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron identified the gangs as Geng Ravi, Geng Kepala, Geng Dany and Geng Mista.
The arrests were made in several operations from Oct 12 by the Temerloh district police Criminal Investigation Division and the Mentakab police crime prevention task force.
Twelve of the suspects tested positive for methamphetamine, while one had 15 previous criminal and drug-related offences, he said in a statement.
Mohd Nasyim said two robberies at ECRL cable storage facilities and five Telekom Malaysia cable thefts were reported in Temerloh, Mentakab and Lanchang between September and October, with losses estimated at RM75,000.
The first operation, conducted from Oct 12 to 15, led to the arrest of five men aged between 20 and 60 in Mentakab, believed to be members of Geng Ravi. Police seized a one-tonne Mitsubishi lorry and several cut metal pole sections. Two other suspects remain at large.
On Oct 14, seven men aged between 30 and 45 were arrested in Kuala Krau and Mentakab in an operation targeting Geng Kepala. Items seized included two four-wheel-drive vehicles, several coils marked "ECRL Property", five cut sections of Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) cable and cable-processing equipment.
On Oct 18, a 28-year-old man believed to be a member of Geng Dany was arrested in Mentakab. He was with a Perodua Myvi, several coils of cable believed to belong to Telekom Malaysia and cable-cutting tools.
The suspect had 15 previous criminal and drug-related offences, and investigations found that the gang had also been active in stealing Telekom Malaysia cables in Kuala Lumpur.
In an operation early today, four men aged between 22 and 31, believed to be members of Geng Mista, were arrested in Bukit Desa Semantan. Police seized a Mitsubishi Triton, several coils of cable, 27 cut sections believed to belong to Telekom Malaysia, and equipment used to pull and cut cables.
All four suspects had previous criminal and drug-related records and tested positive for methamphetamine. The gang's leader was also identified as a member of Geng Kepala, which was busted on Oct 14, while another suspect remains at large.
All suspects have been remanded under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to assist investigations under Sections 395, 379 and 431A of the Penal Code, and Section 235(2) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine got no warning as Russian missiles rain in
Article:
KYIV: Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday, adding that some vital deliveries from the United States were being delayed.
Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine.
Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones in attacks stretching from Kharkiv and Dnipro in the east to Odesa in the south and Volyn and Rivne in the west.
The strikes killed two people in Kyiv and the nearby region and two more people in the industrial city of Kryvyi Rih, officials said.
Tensions are running high between Zelenskyy and President Donald Trump's administration over US support for Ukraine and Washington's approach to Russia.
"Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskyy said on the Telegram app.
"When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defence are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners."
Zelenskyy said that the United States had slowed some vital supplies for Ukraine, adding that the delays were at the US Defence Department level.
He provided no other details. Kyiv has previously said it has struggled to get interceptors critical to repelling Russian missile attacks.
For several months, Ukraine has suffered from critical shortages of US-made Patriot missiles.
Zelenskyy said that some political agreements on air defence were not implemented at a working level.
[[nid:1559274]]
Throughout the nearly five-year war, Ukraine has relied on US intelligence to detect Russian ballistic missile launches and provide early warning of incoming strikes.
Yurii Ihnat, a spokesman for the Ukrainian air force, said Kyiv received no warning ahead of the first ballistic missile strike overnight but did receive information ahead of a second attack.
"For some reason, no information was received the first time, a matter our experts are investigating together with our partners, as this is not the first time such a situation has occurred," Ihnat told Ukrainian television.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that the United States had paused some intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
Ukrainian air defences downed 247 targets - four cruise missiles and 243 drones, the air force said.
Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a "massive strike" using precision weapons and attack drones against Ukrainian defence industry facilities, drone and cruise missile storage sites, and a data centre.
Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said the energy sector was the main target of the attacks, with damage reported across the country.
Ukraine's energy ministry said rolling blackouts were introduced for households and businesses as crews worked to restore supplies.
Koretskyi said Russia has hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure more than 2,000 times since mid-July, intensifying its attacks from previous years of the war.
Railway and metro stations, pharmaceutical warehouses, commercial properties and residential buildings were also damaged, Koretskyi said.
Ukrainian businesses have already lost US$7.7 billion due to wartime damage so far this year, he said.
"The aim is obvious — to wear people down," Koretskyi said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM calls for curfews in France as govt grapples with unrest
Article:
PARIS: France's prime minister called for partial curfews Monday as protesters blocked the entrance to the Louvre in Paris and authorities scrambled to stem public discontent fuelling cost-of-living demonstrations that over the weekend spilled over into some of the worst street violence in recent years.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu did not rule out imposing a state of emergency after the interior minister said the police "had lost control" during the weekend's unrest, which has flared six months before France elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.
With organisers calling for a new round of protests next Saturday, Lecornu called for regional authorities to impose "partial" curfews to protect businesses and people after hundreds of shops were damaged and looted.
"I'm absolutely determined to restore public order", he said, adding that the government was ready to impose a state of emergency "if needed."
Other European countries, where anger over rising prices has also led to protests, were keeping a nervous eye on the developments, with smaller clashes breaking out in Milan, Italy's financial capital, and Belgium over the weekend and protests simmering in Spain and Portugal.
Some half a million people turned out across France on Saturday to denounce the surging cost of living, a culmination of four weeks of protests that began with high school students demanding better conditions at their schools.
What started as peaceful demonstrations morphed into violence in some places, as masked groups on the sidelines of the protests attacked law enforcement, broke into town halls and other public buildings, setting many of them ablaze, looted shops, and set fire to cars, bicycles and scooters on the streets.
More than 2,500 people were arrested and nearly 1,000 members of the security forces injured. Protesters were also hurt, with one demonstrator's hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade.
"On Saturday, in some major cities, you couldn't look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and tell them we hadn't lost control," Nunez said.
[[nid:1559268]]
He said "a number of measures" aimed at containing and preventing looters and vandals would be implemented "starting this evening", including boosting police on the streets.
Macron acknowledged failures in the government response, despite the deployment of some 60,000 law enforcement personnel across the country on Saturday.
Nationwide, more than 2,330 people were taken into police custody over the weekend, 70 percent of whom were adults – and many of whom were already known to authorities, said Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.
At least 3,000 businesses were affected by the unrest, according to Trade and Small Businesses Minister Serge Papin, with damage running into hundreds of millions of euros.
In an address to the nation Sunday, Macron slammed the "unbridled" violence and said local authorities would be able to ban some rallies, but stopped short of imposing more drastic measures.
City authorities in the southern port city of Marseille said they had banned public gatherings from noon to 8pm (1000-1800 GMT).
The European Union slammed the weekend violence as "unacceptable" but warned that the right to peaceful protest "must be protected" in France.
Germany condemned the violence and updated its travel advice for France, saying "further demonstrations and, in some cases, further outbreaks of violence in the coming days cannot be ruled out."
The United Kingdom said the right to protest "can never excuse violence."
In Paris on Monday, about a dozen demonstrators blocked the entrance to the iconic Louvre Museum, the most visited in the world, while puzzled tourists looked on.
"We don't want to get involved. We want to stand back and get away from them," Pat Boland, a tourist from Australia, said of the protests.
"But we don't want to go against them either," his wife Anne added.
[[nid:1559267]]
The two pensioners, both 73, spoke to AFP outside barricades that had been erected at the Louvre, which had closed as a small group of protesters occupied an area outside its famed glass pyramid entrance.
Rising prices have fuelled anger in France, where diesel prices have jumped nearly 40 per cent and petrol by 25 per cent since March, and where food prices have risen by 25 per cent over the past five years.
The unrest has flared just months before presidential elections that will see a new French president elected after a decade of centrist Macron and with Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate for the National Rally party, riding high in the polls.
Ministers and Le Pen have accused ultra-left groups of stoking the violence to boost the chances of the far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon in the presidential polls.
On Monday, Lecornu blamed the "ultra-left movement" for seeking to "orchestrate deep unrest across the country."
"There is a whole network that could be mobilised to even call into question the timetable for the presidential election and the holding of the presidential election itself," Lecornu told reporters.
Melenchon said he was "astonished" at the remarks and said he had "not heard anyone talk about that."
During the weekend, clashes broke out on the sidelines of a cost-of-living demonstration in Milan.
"I'm very worried because it's a new phenomenon, which also originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself," Mayor Giuseppe Sala said.
In Belgium, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in Brussels and Liege.
In Spain protesters have set up tents in the heart of Madrid to denounce soaring housing costs, with similar encampments going up in neighbouring Portugal's main cities of Lisbon and Porto.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No agreement to provide financial support to AirAsia, says government
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial support to low-cost carrier AirAsia amid financial difficulties linked to the Middle East conflict, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance Mminister, said any application for government support from a company in any sector was considered based on the interests of the country and the people, the government's fiscal sustainability and the protection of public funds, in accordance with applicable laws and procedures.
"To date, the government has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial support to AirAsia, whether in the form of guarantees, loans or injections of public funds.
"The government will not comment on speculation or figures reported by the media to avoid affecting the market and the interests of employees, customers and other stakeholders of the companies concerned," he said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament's website today.
He was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong (BN-Ayer Hitam), who asked whether the government was considering providing financial support to the AirAsia Group.
Anwar said the government continuously monitored developments in the country's aviation ecosystem, including the impact of the Middle East crisis, global fuel prices and currency movements on airlines and air connectivity for the people.
He added that the government took note of the issues raised concerning AirAsia, including the losses reported in its latest quarterly financial results, which the low-cost carrier attributed mainly to a sharp increase in jet fuel prices following developments in the Middle East conflict.
"AirAsia is an important part of this ecosystem. In 2025, AirAsia accounted for about 41 per cent of the 104.5 million passenger movements at airports operated by Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd and nearly 60 per cent of domestic passenger movements.
"Much of the air connectivity in Sabah and Sarawak depends on AirAsia flights.
"In 2025, AirAsia carried 62 per cent and 70 per cent of total passengers in Sabah and Sarawak respectively, excluding short take-off and landing (STOL) ports.
"At KLIA Terminal 2, AirAsia carried three-quarters of all passengers," he said.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke had previously said that no meeting had been held between
his ministry and AirAsia
in the past "two or three weeks" amid speculation about potential government support for the low-cost carrier.
However, Loke said any discussions on the matter might have involved the Finance Ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muda unveils 25 policy proposals ahead of GE16
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Muda has launched its Buku 555 campaign, outlining 25 basic policy proposals ahead of the next general election, with a focus on a fairer economy and transparent public spending.
Its president, Amira Aisya Abdul Aziz, said the campaign covered five themes, with estimated costs and funding sources for each proposal.
"The principle behind Buku 555 is simple: a fairer economy for everyone, fully funded. We want economic justice for all Malaysians," she said.
The proposals cover wages and prices, housing and healthcare, family support, skills development and accountable governance.
Amira Aisya said Muda would hold public engagement sessions to gather feedback from workers, families struggling with rental costs and young people facing uncertainty over their career paths.
She said the document would evolve based on public feedback and guide the party's policy advocacy in Parliament, state assemblies and its next election manifesto.
Meanwhile, Muda has decided not to contest the Melaka state election after discussions with its political bureau and party leaders.
The party would instead focus on the 16th general election (GE16) and the Buku 555 campaign to explain its policy priorities and position on 2027 Budget 2027.
Further details on the Melaka election would be announced in a separate media statement or press conference, she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Search for missing 74-year-old woman to expand in Kubang Pasu
Article:
KUBANG PASU: The search for a 74-year-old woman who went missing after leaving her home in Taman Kodiang, Changlun, will continue with a larger team involving several agencies and villagers.
Razaiyah Hassan, who has Alzheimer's disease and high blood pressure, was reported missing by her son at about 2pm yesterday.
Kedah Fire and Rescue Department Zone 1 chief Senior Fire Superintendent Ahmad Aminuddin Abdul Rahim said the department received a call about the missing woman at 2.25pm.
He said 13 personnel from the Bukit Kayu Hitam Fire and Rescue Station were deployed after receiving a briefing from police on the search area.
The search, which included sniffer dogs, covered an area within 500 to 800m, extending to the main road, but no clues were found.
The operation was suspended at 6.30pm, although a small team would continue searching that night. A larger operation involving the Fire and Rescue Department, Civil Defence Force, police and villagers was planned for tomorrow.
Kubang Pasu district police chief Superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said police received a report on the disappearance that day from a 53-year-old man at the Kodiang police station.
He said the woman's son noticed she was missing at about 2.15pm yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Queen donates 500,000 face masks to Johor schoolchildren
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, today donated 500,000 face masks to the Johor state government for distribution to schoolchildren across the state.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page, the masks were donated through the Raja Zarith Sofiah of Johor Foundation (YRZSNJ).
Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor was also present at the ceremony, held at the Johor City Council Tower Auditorium Hall.
The contribution is part of the Queen's ongoing efforts to support communities affected by the haze.
Also present were Johor State Secretary Datuk Mohammed Ridha Abd Kadir, state Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali, Johor Deputy State Secretary Datuk Nasri Md Ali and Johor Education Department director Zulkurnain Abdul Rahman.
Her Majesty had previously donated nearly 300,000 face masks for frontline personnel, including those from the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency and the police, as well as for distribution across all districts in Johor.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor PWD to add lane at accident-prone Alam Budiman junction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor Public Works Department (PWD) plans to add a lane at the traffic light junction in Alam Budiman, Shah Alam, following recurring accidents involving heavy vehicles, particularly lorries.
Its director, Shukri Ishak, told Buletin Utama TV3 that survey and utility mapping works were planned to begin at the site in about two weeks.
The medium-term measure will involve building an additional lane about 300m long from the Shah Alam direction, as well as improving street lighting and traffic lights at the junction, he said.
The department has previously introduced several safety measures at the location, including a temporary lane, road signs and improved lighting.

Title: Haze: Indonesia puts offers from Malaysia, others to combat forest fires on hold [WATCH]
Article:
JAKARTA: Foreign assistance, including from Malaysia, to help Indonesia combat widespread forest and land fires will have to wait as the republic has yet to declare the situation a national disaster.
Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Dudung Abdurachman said the Indonesian government remained confident in its ability to manage the crisis using its own resources.
"For now, we are still capable. Our country is still capable," he told a press conference on Monday.
Acknowledging Malaysia's offer of assistance, he said help would be forthcoming if the situation were declared a national disaster.
"It is not a question of assistance, but there are also many technical challenges on the ground, including fuel distribution and other logistical issues," he said.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reaffirmed Malaysia's readiness to assist Indonesia and said Malaysia had proposed an Asean-level cooperation mechanism to strengthen coordination, preparedness and collective action against transboundary haze.
Earlier today, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi reiterated Malaysia's readiness to mobilise assets, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 50 personnel, pending official approval from Indonesia.
The offer was first made during Zahid's meeting with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in Hambalang, West Java, on Sept 18. Prabowo welcomed the offer.
On Oct 15, Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir was quoted as saying that Prabowo had approved offers of assistance from neighbouring countries to help combat the widespread forest and land fires, and that the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) was holding technical-level discussions on implementation.

Title: 6 arrested after Indonesian woman rescued with burns
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Six men, including an employer, have been arrested after police rescued an Indonesian woman who was abused and left with burns across her body.
The arrests followed a police raid at a tyre shop in Jalan Merbau, Pusat Perniagaan Oren.
Seberang Prai Utara district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman said the operation was linked to a case reported in Tanjong Sepat, Selangor.
"The victim sustained burn injuries across her body," he said.
The operation was carried out by the Selangor police contingent's Criminal Investigation Department, together with the Kuala Langat district police Criminal Investigation Division, with assistance from the Penang police forensic team.
The alleged incident took place in Selangor. The Indonesian victim was rescued on Oct 16.
The case is being investigated under Section 12 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (Act 670).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB, PTP in strategic partnership to power Malaysia's net-zero aspiration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) has entered into a strategic partnership with Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), a member of the MMC Group, to support Malaysia's decarbonisation agenda and enhance sustainability compliance via greater renewable energy (RE) adoption under the Green Electricity Tariff (GET) programme.
In a joint statement today, they said the partnership brings together TNB's access to certified RE and PTP's strong commitment to decarbonising its operations, demonstrating how existing national infrastructure can support businesses in advancing their sustainability goals and reducing emissions.
"Under the partnership, PTP subscribed to 16,000 blocks of GET, equivalent to 16GWh of certified green energy per month, for the period from May 2026 to December 2027," the statement said.
"The subscription makes PTP the largest GET subscriber among Malaysian ports to date and enables the port to transition its electricity supply to 100 per cent RE."
The GET programme allows TNB customers to power their premises with certified RE. Subscribers pay a normal base tariff plus a tiered green premium, and receive annual Malaysia Renewable Energy Certificates (mREC).
NEW BENCHMARK FOR SUSTAINABLE MARITIME OPERATIONS
Through the GET programme, PTP will receive certificates that correspond to its green energy subscription. This will support its sustainable strategy, which targets a 45 per cent reduction in carbon emissions by 2030, and ultimately achieving net zero by 2050, in line with national target.
PTP's GET adoption reinforces its position as a sustainable global transshipment hub and sets a new benchmark for RE adoption within Malaysia's maritime and logistics sector.
The partnership also serves as a guiding model for other energy-intensive infrastructure operators, demonstrating how businesses can leverage certified RE through the existing grid to accelerate their sustainability journey.
TNB chief retail officer Datuk Kamal Arifin A. Rahman presented a symbolic GET subscription certificate to PTP chief executive officer (CEO) Mark Hardiman, witnessed by TNB president/CEO Datuk Seri Shamsul Ahmad.
Shamsul said TNB remains committed to enabling more businesses to participate in Malaysia's transition towards a cleaner and more sustainable energy system by providing access to RE solutions that support both environmental goals and long-term business competitiveness.
"Our partnership serves as a powerful catalyst for the entire maritime and logistics sector to embrace energy transition, especially in supporting Malaysia's accelerated efforts to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 as aspired in the National Energy Transition Roadmap.
"This commitment demonstrates how Malaysia's businesses can play a meaningful role in advancing the nation's energy transition while strengthening the competitiveness of key economic sectors," he said.
Hardiman said the subscription is both a contractual agreement and a declaration of PTP's intent to lead the maritime industry toward a more sustainable future.
"By integrating GET into our operations, we are accelerating our transition to renewable energy and taking a decisive step toward our 2030 carbon reduction targets. This initiative proves that operational excellence and environmental stewardship are not mutually exclusive, but in fact, the dual engines that will drive PTP's long-term growth and resilience in a changing global landscape.
"The adoption of the GET programme allows PTP to directly support the growth of RE generation in Malaysia, ensuring that its massive terminal operations are powered by cleaner, greener energy sources," he added.
ADVANCING MALAYSIA'S GREEN GROWTH
The partnership contributes to Malaysia's broader efforts to accelerate RE adoption and reduce carbon emissions across the economy, particularly in energy-intensive sectors critical to national trade and economic growth.
As a key economic hub in Johor, PTP's adoption of GET also supports the state's broader green economy ambitions and strengthens the role of major infrastructure operators in advancing sustainable growth, while reinforcing TNB's position as a partner in the decarbonisation of Malaysia's critical infrastructure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-delivery rider jailed 30 years for meth trafficking
Article:
AYER KEROH: A former p-hailing delivery rider was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane by the Ayer Keroh High Court after being found guilty of trafficking 684g of methamphetamine five years ago.
Judge Datuk DJP Suria Kumar sentenced Muhammad Nadhir Zailany, 31, after finding that the defence had failed to raise reasonable doubt over the prosecution's case.
The judge said the defence had questioned the prosecution's failure to call a man known as "Hafiz", whom the accused claimed was the actual owner of the drugs, as well as its failure to call Inspector Hasif as a witness.
"The prosecution's failure to call Hafiz as a witness did not undermine the testimony of the fourth and fifth prosecution witnesses, who saw the bag containing the drugs on the accused's body. This showed that he had control, knowledge and possession of the drugs," Suria said.
He said the accused had driven a Proton Preve for almost 15 hours from Kota Warisan to Sentul before heading towards the Ayer Keroh Toll Plaza, with the bag slung across his body. He was alone in the car when it was stopped.
The court found that the accused had used a forged employment confirmation letter to deceive authorities checking travel documents during the movement control order.
Suria said the defence had failed to rebut the presumption of drug trafficking or raise reasonable doubt over the prosecution's case.
The sentence was backdated to his arrest on June 9, 2021.

Title: Malaysian recounts harrowing walk through Paris protests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian businessman was forced to walk four kilometres through tear gas and street fires after train services were suspended during protests in Paris, France, turning his journey back to the hotel into a harrowing experience.
Mohd Izdiharuddin Sulaiman, managing director of Royal Chef Products (M) Sdn Bhd, said he was caught in the unrest near the Champs-Élysées on Saturday after train services ground to a halt.
"That was the first time I was right in the middle of a riot area.
"I went right through the protests with tear gas, fires and everything. The police were tackling protesters, but they didn't bother me because I was wearing a suit, so they didn't view me as a threat."
Izdiharuddin was in Paris under the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) to participate in Salon International de l'Alimentation (SIAL Paris 2026), an international food and beverage exhibition.
[[nid:1559207]]
Despite the unrest, he said he would proceed with his scheduled business meetings at the exhibition, adding that his daily journeys between the hotel and exhibition centre remained relatively safe.
"My family was concerned and asked if I could fly back earlier, but my flight is scheduled as planned.
"My daily travel between the hotel and exhibition centre feels pretty safe, though police presence increases late at night."
He said that although social media reports showed widespread destruction, the damage he saw in Paris was largely confined to smaller retail outlets.
"On my way back, I saw a few small clothing and accessory shops broken into, but not major luxury brand stores. Some luxury brand stores are safe because of heavy security and bulletproof glass," he said.
He added that municipal cleanup crews had cleared away street debris by Monday morning.
Another Malaysian exhibitor, Farmers River International Sdn Bhd managing director Zaini Rahman, said the protests had not disrupted the SIAL Paris exhibition, as the venue was located near the airport on the outskirts of the city.
He said Malaysian delegates attending the food fair remained safe, with the unrest largely confined to central Paris.
"The demonstrations and riots are happening in central Paris. Our venue is far from the commotion, so it has not affected us," he said.
Zaini said 50 Malaysian companies had sent between 100 and 120 delegates, mostly from the food and beverage sector, and all were safe and accounted for.
He said that while central Paris had experienced tense moments over the weekend, protesters were avoiding international business venues and foreign visitors.
"Police are everywhere, especially at central train stations we use to commute. Venue security is also strict, thoroughly checking badges and identity cards," he said.
He added that the Malaysian Embassy had registered all local delegates and issued safety advisories urging them to avoid high-risk protest zones.
Although social media portrayed the situation as chaotic, Zaini said the unrest was localised, and the exhibition had drawn a large crowd of potential buyers after a quieter weekend.
"Social media makes it look chaotic overall, but the unrest is localised to specific areas. Weekend turnout was lower, but the exhibition floor is now very crowded with potential buyers," he said.
The Malaysian delegation is scheduled to return home on Friday.

Title: IHH Healthcare Malaysia expands Gleneagles Hospital Johor with Afiniti Wellness acquisition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Pantai Medical Centre Sdn Bhd, has entered into an agreement to acquire Afiniti Wellness in Medini, Iskandar Puteri, Johor, laying the foundation for an integrated healthcare campus spanning approximately 18 acres.
The acquired property will be developed into a dedicated Ambulatory Care Centre (ACC) for consultations, diagnostics, day surgery, and other outpatient services. The move forms a key part of Gleneagles Hospital Johor's next phase in Medini.
Moving selected outpatient and daycase services to a dedicated setting will provide patients with more convenient access to treatment that does not require admission, while allowing Gleneagles Johor to optimize its existing infrastructure for patients requiring higher-acuity and more complex care.
The expansion comes as Johor prepares for the upcoming Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), a priority sector of which is healthcare. Demand for quality care is expected to grow alongside the JS-SEZ, which is set to accelerate the movement of people, talent, and investment along the Johor-Singapore corridor.
Dr Kamal Amzan, chief executive officer of IHH Healthcare Malaysia, said:
"Johor is entering an important period of growth with establishment of the JS-SEZ, and Gleneagles Johor is ready to support the state's rising healthcare needs," said Dr Kamal Amzan, chief executive officer of IHH Healthcare Malaysia.
He added IHH is committed to long-term investment in Gleneagles Johor.
"For IHH Healthcare Malaysia, the opportunity is not simply to become bigger. It is to build greater clinical depth where it is needed and ensure patients can access increasingly sophisticated care closer to home," Dr Kamal added.
Together with IHH Healthcare Malaysia's existing landbank in Medini, the planned healthcare campus is expected to support approximately 350 inpatient beds upon completion of the ACC.
A further 150-bed inpatient block is currently under evaluation as part of the hospital's longer-term plans for tertiary and quaternary care.
Since opening in 2015, Gleneagles Johor has delivered more than 1.7 million inpatient, daycare, and outpatient episodes of care. Over 100 specialists and more than 1,200 healthcare professionals provide care at the hospital across key specialties including Oncology, Cardiology, Orthopaedics, Neuroscience, and Women & Children's Health.
Gleneagles Johor's clinical capabilities include da Vinci robotic-assisted surgery, robotic-assisted joint replacement systems, PET-CT, LINAC, and other specialized diagnostic and treatment platforms.

Title: Kelantan folks say ECRL fares are reasonable
Article:
KOTA BARU: The people in Kelantan have described the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) fares of RM125 to RM147 for journeys between Gombak and Kota Baru as reasonable, given the shorter travel time.
They said the service, scheduled to begin commercial operations in mid-December, would give them more transport options for travelling to the Klang Valley.
Resident Fiza Abdul Rahim, 38, said the fare announcement was eagerly awaited by the people in the state.
"We have been waiting for the fares for the past few months, and today we finally have the answer. I think fares of between RM125 and RM147 are reasonable.
"Although they are slightly more expensive than express bus fares, the journey takes only four hours, compared with eight hours by bus.
"I am confident that demand for the ECRL service will be encouraging when it begins operations in December. More importantly, the people in Kelantan will have a wider choice of transport," she said.
It was reported that
ECRL fares
would start at RM125 for an Economy Class transit service between Gombak and Kota Baru.
Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said the government had approved the proposed fare structure on Oct 16, based on a dynamic pricing mechanism.
Muhammad Azrin Zainal Abidin, deputy chairman of the Malaysian Association of Hotels' Kelantan chapter, also described the fares as reasonable, saying the service could attract more tourists to the state while making travel to the Klang Valley more convenient for the people in Kelantan.
He suggested that fares be adjusted according to the day of travel, with lower prices on weekdays than on weekends and public holidays.
"Airlines and express bus operators also adopt this approach.
"However, I would say the fares are within expectations and are not too expensive when compared with the journey time," he said.
Kelantan People's Action Council president Aiman Yusri Mohd Yusoff also considered the fares reasonable, given the journey time and service provided.
He acknowledged that reactions to the announcement were mixed, with some describing the fares as expensive and others calling for lower prices.
"However, I believe they are reasonable given the journey time, with fares starting from as low as RM125.
"I am confident that, in addition to attracting tourists to Kelantan, the service will encourage the people in the state to travel to the Klang Valley more often. Some may even make day trips without staying overnight," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAB Cakaran teaming up with Oiltek in palm oil-based animal feed ingredients
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CAB Cakaran Corp Bhd is teaming up with Oiltek Global Pte Ltd to explore a joint venture to develop premium animal feed ingredients from palm oil-derived products.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, CAB Cakaran said the proposed collaboration combines its expertise in animal nutrition, feedmill operations and livestock production with Oiltek Global's palm oil processing technologies.
"The parties believe there is a significant market opportunity for high-quality, cost-effective and nutritionally enhanced palm-derived feed ingredients addressing a gap in the current feed market while supporting sustainable utilisation of palm-based resources," the company said.
Oiltek Global, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Singapore-listed Oiltek International Ltd, will contribute its proprietary technology, processing know-how and engineering capabilities.
It will also provide expertise in palm oil refining, waste-to-value processes and downstream product development.
CAB Cakaran, meanwhile, intends to support the collaboration through its existing feedmill infrastructure, processing capacity, supply chain relationships and distribution network.
The parties plan to establish a joint venture company in Malaysia to develop and commercialise the palm-derived feed products, subject to the completion of technical, commercial and regulatory assessments, as well as the necessary approvals.
The proposed joint venture's shareholding structure has yet to be finalised.
CAB Cakaran said the collaboration could open new market opportunities, support more sustainable use of palm-based resources and diversify its income streams, potentially contributing positively to its future profitability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL20 startup investments generate RM202.64bil in sales proceeds since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Investments in startups since the launch of KL20 in 2024 have generated total sales proceeds of RM202.64 billion, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
He said investments channelled into the startup ecosystem amounted to about RM50 billion since 2024.
Akmal Nasrullah said Malaysia aimed to attract about RM700 million in venture capital investments and add between 2,000 and 3,500 active startups by 2030 through the KL20 initiative.
"This is why we are seeing positive developments in efforts to develop the startup ecosystem," he told reporters after a fireside chat titled "From Action Plan to Activation" at KL20 2026 here today.
On the government's target of producing five unicorn companies by 2030, Akmal Nasrullah said the government was still working to strengthen the startup ecosystem.
Relevant agencies are assisting in identifying and developing promising companies at all stages of growth, said the minister, adding that this was an ongoing process requiring cooperation among agencies to support startups from their early stages until they were capable of achieving unicorn status.
"We are not merely setting a target of producing unicorn companies, but also seeking to transform the economic structure, particularly by creating high-value jobs and increasing their contribution to the national economy.
"At the same time, the aspiration to produce local companies with global recognition will remain a priority," said Akmal Nasrullah.

Title: Propel Global proposes diversification into property development to revive earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Propel Global Bhd had proposed to diversify its core operations to include property development, entering a new sector as it seeks to rebuild profitability following two consecutive years of steep net losses.
The group, which currently operates across oil and gas, technical services, and information and communications technology, aims to establish a fresh income stream through its maiden commercial property development project in Pahang.
The proposed diversification is expected to provide Propel Global with an additional source of revenue and earnings, thereby reducing its reliance on its existing business segments.
"The property development business is also complementary to the group's existing technical services segment, allowing the group to leverage its experience in engineering, construction and project management in undertaking property development projects.
"In addition, the proposed diversification would enable the group to participate in the development and sale of properties, thereby broadening the group's business activities and providing opportunities for long term growth," said Propel Global in an exchange filing.
After generating a net profit of RM7.62 million on RM110.89 million in revenue for the financial year ended June 30, 2023 (FY23), and a net profit of RM5.71 million on RM176.04 million in revenue for FY24, the group's financial trajectory reversed sharply.
For FY25, revenue contracted to RM111.5 million, resulting in a net loss of RM24.2 million. Top-line contractions persisted into FY26, with unaudited revenue dropping to RM80.38 million and net losses widening further to RM27.21 million.
Management attributed the downturn across its existing divisions to a combination of factors.
The oil and gas segment experienced lower progress billings from several major engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning contracts, alongside lower radial cutting torch services and the absence of production chemicals income following a subsidiary disposal.
Meanwhile, revenue from technical services fell sharply due to slower project execution, lower progress recognition, and the completion of key contracts from prior cycles, while newly secured contracts remained in early execution phases.
The ICT division similarly saw earnings moderate following reduced billings for one-off maintenance and repair services.
To spearhead its real estate strategy, its subsidiary Propel Global Development Sdn Bhd had acquired two adjoining freehold land parcels in Kuantan for RM14.7 million cash from Goldhill Deluxe Sdn Bhd in October 2023.
The site is being developed into a commercial project known as Riverpoint, which will feature 31 units of three-storey freehold shop lots designed for retail, food and beverage, and office use.
Propel Global projects the development to yield a gross development value of RM64.0 million against estimated gross development costs of RM53.0 million, translating to an expected gross development profit of RM11.0 million.
Planning permission for Riverpoint was secured in November 2024, followed by building plan approval in July 2025.
The project is slated for launch in December 2026, with completion targeted for January 2028 under an estimated 13-month timeline. Funding will be sourced through a combination of internal funds and bank borrowings.
Following the Riverpoint project, the group intends to evaluate and pursue suitable property development opportunities from time to time, subject to prevailing market conditions and the availability of suitable development lands.
The group's entry into real estate is led by Chia Hiap Wei, General Manager of Propel Global Development. Chia joined the group in 2023 bringing over two decades of real estate and project management experience across Malaysia and Australia.
His career includes managing residential and commercial developments at TA Properties and TA Global Bhd, such as Idaman Residence, Damansara Avenue, and Nova Square, as well as hotel refurbishments in Sydney and Melaka.
He subsequently served as deputy senior project manager at UEM Sunrise Bhd, leading land acquisitions in Cheras, Mont Kiara, and Equine Park, alongside managing commercial developments in Kuala Lumpur and Johor.
Under Bursa Malaysia's Main Market Listing Requirements, any transaction expected to divert 25 percent or more of a listed company's net assets to a new line of business, or contribute 25 percent or more to net profits, requires prior shareholder approval.
Consequently, Propel Global will convene an extraordinary general meeting to seek shareholder authorization for the diversification proposal.
In its disclosure, the group highlighted several risk factors, including its lack of an established track record in property development compared to major industry incumbents with larger land banks.
Other operational risks encompass potential project delays, regulatory clearance timelines, raw material and labor cost fluctuations, and heightened leverage associated with capital-intensive development work.
The proposed diversification does not involve any issuance of new ordinary shares, meaning it will have no immediate impact on Propel Global's issued share capital, substantial shareholders' stakes, net asset per share, or earnings per share.
Barring unforeseen delays, the diversification will take effect immediately upon receiving shareholder approval at the upcoming extraordinary general meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3,000 Malaysians in France safe amid nationwide protests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All 3,000 Malaysians registered with the Malaysian embassy in France are safe and accounted for amid ongoing nationwide protests, says Malaysian Ambassador to France Datuk Eldeen Husaini Mohd Hashim.
Eldeen said major cities, including Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Lille, had seen large demonstrations, with the number of protesters estimated at between 500,000 and 600,000.
Despite the large turnouts, no Malaysians had been injured or caught up in the unrest, he said.
"As of today, we have around 3,000 Malaysians registered with us in France, including about 300 in Paris and the rest scattered all over. They are mostly students and those working here.
"We are continuously monitoring the situation and contacting our citizens here. As far as we know, there are no injuries and no Malaysians involved in the protests," he told the New Straits Times.
He said the embassy was working closely with French authorities, city hall and the Foreign Ministry to monitor developments and provide assistance.
Eldeen said he had also witnessed a group of young demonstrators while attending an event in central Paris.
"I was walking after attending a forum near the Champs-Élysées when hundreds of protesters rushed through the streets. Most of them were younger, mainly university students.
"While there was concern on my part if the demonstration turned violent, the situation at the time did not escalate into a riot. Champs-Élysées remained relatively safe, though it was unfortunate that a group chose that area to gather."
He added that the demonstrations could continue in the coming days.
"I cannot say if the worst has passed because these protests are ongoing. The demand started over student frustration with the education system, but it has since expanded to cost-of-living issues, gas prices and fuel costs.
"The French government, including the president and prime minister, has publicly addressed the public to calm the situation."
Eldeen advised Malaysians residing in or visiting France to remain vigilant, avoid high-risk protest areas and keep in touch with diplomatic officials.
"For those living in France, the best advice is to completely avoid protest areas unless absolutely necessary. For tourists planning holidays, monitor the situation closely and consider rescheduling non-essential travel until things settle.
"Most importantly, we strongly urge all Malaysian travellers and tourists in France to register with the embassy. Knowing where you are makes it much easier for us to communicate and assist you if you run into trouble."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Government mulls eKYC, age verification for online gaming platforms, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will examine the feasibility of extending electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) and age verification requirements to online gaming platforms such as Roblox.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the move would take into account various aspects, including underage users and the possibility of the platforms being misused by extremist, radical and terrorist groups.
"In my discussions with Roblox, for example, since last year, it has shown that it is ready to cooperate.
"The issue might only be in terms of user verification and age verification.
"So we will look into the suitability of extending eKYC and age verification to platforms like Roblox," he told reporters after the document exchange ceremony for a RM5.2 billion financing facility for Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) here today.
He was commenting on a statement by former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay on the issue, which also involves underage children.
Fahmi said the government, including through the National Security Council, continuously monitors platforms that could be misused by such groups.
He said the authorities, including the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), would take action if necessary.
"We will consider various aspects, but if prompt action needs to be taken, that will certainly be carried out by the authorities," he said.
In another development, Fahmi said he would discuss age restrictions for social media users with his Indonesian counterpart during a visit to the country.
He is scheduled to leave for Bali before heading to Jakarta tomorrow to attend the World Conference on Creative Economy (WCCE) 2026 and hold a series of meetings, including with ministers responsible for communications and digital affairs, as well as culture.
"Indonesia has its own approaches and regulatory framework, and there are differences and similarities with Malaysia.
"We will discuss the challenges faced in engaging with social media platform service providers," he said.
Fahmi added that a meeting with Indonesia's Minister of Culture would also discuss Malaysia's aspiration to make local intellectual property (IP) available to Indonesian audiences.
He said Malaysian works streamed on platforms such as Viu were also watched by audiences in the neighbouring country.
He said both sides would explore ways to strengthen ties between Malaysia's and Indonesia's film industries, as well as discuss productions and online content.
"We will also discuss collaborative efforts between production companies, films and creative content," he said.

Title: MMAG disposes a freighter aircraft at RM12.7mil loss
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MMAG Holdings Bhd, through its indirect unit MJets Air Sdn Bhd, is disposing of a Boeing B737-400SF converted freighter for US$2.8 million (RM11.43 million), as part of its ongoing review of its aviation assets and operations.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the group said MJets Air had entered into an aircraft purchase agreement with Mont Gabanon Airlines on Oct 19.
MMAG said ongoing geopolitical tensions, global uncertainty and a sharp rise in fuel prices had significantly increased operating costs and weakened charter demand.
It added that demand for this aircraft model was insufficient to generate revenue to cover its operating costs, making it a financial burden to the group.
The aircraft was acquired by MJets Air on Jan 24, 2025, for US$6.55 million.
Based on its unaudited net book value of RM24.12 million as at Sept 30, 2026, the disposal is expected to result in a loss of RM12.69 million.
"The proceeds received from the proposed disposal will be mainly used for MJets Air's working capital requirement, including but not limited to the payment of trade and other payables, operating expenses, lease rental and other day-to-day business expenditures.
"The utilisation of proceeds will enable MJets Air to support its ongoing operations and manage its working capital requirements," it said.
Under the agreement, the buyer will pay an earnest deposit of US$1 million before inspecting the aircraft, followed by the remaining US$1.8 million upon satisfactory completion of the inspection.
The aircraft will be delivered to a mutually agreed location outside Malaysia, with completion expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, barring unforeseen circumstances.
"The board is of the view that the proposed disposal is in the best interests of the company, as the continued retention of the aircraft is not commercially viable in the absence of any viable deployment plans.
"In view of the above, the proposed disposal will enable the group to reduce its financial burden and streamline its aviation operations," MMAG said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UM student who questioned donations to Najib stands by remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya student Ummi Umairah Bakhit will not retract her remarks about public donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which she made at a summit here recently.
She reiterated that she would not apologise for the remarks, which sparked debate among various quarters.
"I stand by the question I asked and will not apologise. I hope more people will find the courage to speak up about corruption and integrity without fear," she said in a post on her Instagram account today.
Ummi said her views remained unchanged and that she remained committed to the principles of integrity, equality and justice, as well as opposing corruption.
"I have never picked and chosen which issues to fight for. I attended the demonstration against (former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission chief commissioner Tan Sri) Azam Baki.
"I have also spoken out about inequality of opportunities at my university. From day one, I have been consistent in my stance," she said.
Ummi also expressed disappointment with the reactions of some members of the public, which she described as being influenced by cyberbullying, political obsession and a feudal mentality.
"Describing an act as stupid is not an offence under the law. It is a strong expression used to describe an act that is unbelievable or makes no sense.
"Critical thinking is increasingly eroding. People read, but they do not think, conduct research or understand what they read. The context is distorted.
"Describing an act as stupid is not the same as calling someone stupid," she said.
Ummi recently said she had faced
online harassment and threats
after videos of her remarks at the event went viral.
She, however, insisted that she would not be intimidated by the attacks, saying she believed it was her responsibility to challenge public perceptions, particularly among young people.
It was reported that Ummi raised the issue during a dialogue with former minister Khairy Jamaluddin, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
She questioned public donations to Najib, citing his legal cases linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and his conviction in the SRC International case.
"The stupidest thing I have watched in my entire life is people donating to our former prime minister, Najib Razak, someone who clearly has a worldwide corruption case, 1MDB, and is clearly linked to corruption," she said.
Ummi also raised the Tabung Haji controversy and sought the panellists' views on corruption and political accountability.
